title: Experimenting with input formats and writing styles

videos.script: Change two things at once, and a number can only tell you that something changed. {{title}} Here is the triage prompt written two ways. One lists its fields as bullets. The other says the same things in a paragraph. {{diff}} Run both on seventy messages and the totals are a tie, twenty-six to twenty-seven. The sign test calls it chance. {{check}} Look closer. Twelve categories changed. And the urgency mistakes switched sides: the bullets called too much urgent, the paragraph too little. {{answers}} The sign test was right about the total. You need six changed messages, all going the same way, before it calls anything unlikely to be chance, and a split of seven to six never will. {{sign}} Now run the paragraph again with a temperature left in the command. The totals look much the same, and you cannot tell which change did what. {{confound}} By the end of this lesson you can design an experiment that changes one thing, report what it found beneath the total, and choose the format of the data you put in a prompt. {{close}}
